Kelvin must identify the order of the pads one position at a time. For position k (k = 1 to 10), there are 11 − k candidate pads left.

**Cost of the wrong guesses.** In the worst case, Kelvin guesses wrong 10 − k times at position k. Each wrong guess costs k hops: k − 1 hops along the already-known pads, plus 1 hop onto the wrong pad. The last remaining candidate is known by elimination, so he never has to test it.

Total hops lost to wrong guesses:

Σ_{k=1}^{10} (10 − k)·k = 10·55 − 385 = 165.

**Cost of the final successful run.** Once the full order is known, he hops across all 10 pads and then onto the far bank, which is 11 hops.

Worst-case total: 165 + 11 = 176.

ANSWER: 176
